subject: chemistry

moments.title: Markovnikov's rule
moments.body: Markovnikov publishes a rule for HX addition to alkenes: H adds to the C with more Hs already. The rule is dismissed by Western chemists for years because it appears in Russian journals.
moments.takeaway: A regioselectivity rule, hidden in Russian literature for a generation.

moments.title: Mechanism explained
moments.body: Whitmore explains Markovnikov in terms of carbocation stability. The more stable carbocation forms, controlling the addition.
moments.takeaway: A rule of observation gets a mechanistic basis.

moments.title: Hydroboration
moments.body: Brown develops hydroboration-oxidation, giving anti-Markovnikov hydration of alkenes. He wins the 1979 Nobel.

moments.title: Selective synthesis
moments.body: Modern catalysts let synthetic chemists choose Markovnikov or anti-Markovnikov at will. The 'rule' is now a starting point, not a constraint.
moments.takeaway: Selectivity is now a tunable parameter.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Markovnikov is taught at A-level and IB. The underlying carbocation logic predicts countless other reactions.
now.open_questions: Can we control regiochemistry, stereochemistry and chemoselectivity in arbitrary reactions?

reflection: Markovnikov's rule was dismissed for years because it was in Russian. How does language barrier still distort science today?
